Colours for three-part compositions, as on CensusMapper

Source: R/cm_tricolore.R
cm_tricolore.Rd

Colours for compositions of three parts, e.g. the shares of children, working age population and seniors, with the balance scheme of the tricolore package, as used by CensusMapper's ternary ("rgb") maps. The colours are the same as tricolore::Tricolore()'s, with the parameters in CensusMapper's units, the same as in a CensusMapper map's tricolore_options.

Usage

cm_tricolore(
  p1,
  p2,
  p3,
  center = rep(1/3, 3),
  breaks = 3,
  hue = 60,
  chroma = 200,
  lightness = 80,
  contrast = 0.4,
  spread = 1
)

Arguments

p1, p2, p3

The three parts, as counts or shares; they are divided by their total. Compositions with missing or negative parts, or a total of zero, get NA.

center

The composition that gets the neutral (grey) colour, e.g. the composition of the whole region. By default the centre of the triangle.

breaks

The number of breaks along each side of the triangle for discrete colours, Inf for continuous colours.

hue

The hue of the first part, in degrees (0 to 360); the other parts are 120 and 240 degrees further.

chroma

The maximum chroma (CIE-LUV, 0 to 200). Above about 75 some colours are outside the sRGB gamut and are clipped.

lightness

The lightness (0 to 100).

contrast

How much less light and chroma compositions near the centre get (0 to 1).

spread

How spread out the colours are around the centre (> 0).

Value

A character vector of colours ("#RRGGBB"), one for each composition.

Details

With discrete colours (finite breaks) the triangle of compositions is split into breaks^2 triangles, and each composition gets the colour of the centroid of its triangle. The center changes the colours of these triangles, but not their shape.

References

Schöley, J. (2021). The centered ternary balance scheme: A technique to visualize surfaces of unbalanced three-part compositions. Demographic Research, 44(19), 443–458. doi:10.4054/DemRes.2021.44.19

See also

geom_cm_tricolore() for a ggplot map with these colours and a colour key.

Examples

cm_tricolore(c(0.2, 0.5, 1), c(0.6, 0.3, 1), c(0.2, 0.2, 1))
#> [1] "#009F92" "#A8894C" "#C37787"
